solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Great clue to start — 16

indicators.note: to start asks for only the opening letter of the word clue

parts.note: 16 across is SHELVES, read as a noun: a set of shelves is racking

explanation.surface: A setter boasts that the very first clue of the puzzle is a beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference sends you to 16 across, whose answer is read here as a plural noun, not the verb used in that clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracking is British informal praise meaning excellent, a synonym of great.

clue.text: Negligent US state holds America back

indicators.note: holds means the state abbreviation contains the other piece

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation of California

indicators.note: back reverses the word for America

parts.note: USA is America

explanation.surface: A careless state keeps America from moving forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual means offhand or careless, a synonym of negligent.

clue.text: A god, one filling application for licence

definitions.note: used here as a verb, to permit

indicators.note: filling means the god and one go inside the word for application

parts.note: application is use
Thor is the Norse god of thunder
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A deity applies for a licence on a form.
explanation.definitionFit: To license someone is to grant permission, i.e. officially sanction.

clue.text: Cut drug informer up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces are read bottom to top

parts.note: E is ecstasy
a fink is an informer

explanation.surface: An informant on drugs is caught out.
explanation.definitionFit: To knife someone is to stab or cut them with a blade.

clue.text: Sadly one runs around bound to be a failure

indicators.note: around means those letters go around the leap
sadly signals that the letters of one are upset

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a bound is a hop

explanation.surface: A doomed runner keeps lapping the track, sure to lose.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hoper is someone with no chance of success, a loser.

clue.text: Second not so good — 14

parts.note: of lower quality, i.e. worse

explanation.surface: Someone ranked second is judged a little less impressive than the winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 across is DIMMER, meaning less intelligent; slower has that same sense of being less quick-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are comparatives meaning less mentally quick, a synonym pair for stupidity.

clue.text: She washes underpants? Girl's clothing

indicators.note: clothing means the girl wraps around the jumbled letters

parts.note: a lass is a girl

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, signalling under is messed up

explanation.surface: A washerwoman handles underwear among a girl's clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A laundress is a woman employed to wash clothes and linen.

clue.text: With new sandwich fish spread

indicators.note: sandwich means the two abbreviations go either side of the fish

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Fish paste is spread in a fresh sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: To widen is to broaden or spread out.

clue.text: Fully behind branch opening store after renovation

indicators.note: opening means the branch is set into the middle of the shop letters
after renovation shows the letters of store are rebuilt

parts.note: an arm is a branch

explanation.surface: A branch opens a store once it has been refurbished.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearmost means at the very back, completely behind the others.

clue.text: Go nowhere as one races into view

indicators.note: into shows the pieces for one and races going inside the word for view

parts.note: a view is a sight
one is I, the Roman numeral
the TT races are the motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A spectator stays put as a runner sprints into sight.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay where you are and wait is an idiom for going nowhere.

clue.text: God had rotten old fruit first

indicators.note: first puts the friendly term ahead of the jumbled word

parts.note: old fruit is a jovial British form of address, like bud for a pal

indicators.note: rotten signals that the letters of had are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A deity enjoyed some decaying fruit before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: The Buddha is revered as a divine figure in some traditions, loosely a god.

clue.text: God, how some mimic the French — and those opposing them

parts.note: mock French accents say ze for the
us versus them

explanation.surface: Asks how people imitate the French and those who oppose them.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus is the king of the Greek gods.

clue.text: Came to wonder about 2

indicators.note: about means the word for wonder goes around the cross-referenced piece

parts.note: wonder is awe
2 down is AUTHORISE, and to okay something is to authorise it

explanation.surface: Someone regains consciousness puzzling over a cross-referenced clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Came to means regained consciousness, past tense of waking up.

clue.text: Perhaps Cinephile rejected subscription that breaks £25/minute

indicators.note: that breaks means the reversed fee goes inside the slang money term

parts.note: a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds

indicators.note: rejected signals the fee word is turned back to front

parts.note: a subscription is dues paid

explanation.surface: A film fan cancels a subscription costing twenty-five pounds a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: Cinephile was the crossword name used by the setter Araucaria, an example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinephile is a setter's assumed byline, an example of a false name.

clue.text: "I am what I am", doctor admits, making a sort of switch

indicators.note: admits shows the doctor abbreviation taking the other letters inside

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
what I am is me

explanation.surface: A doctor lets in a patient who declares their identity, then flicks a switch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I Am What I Am' looks like a quoted song title, but it splits into two pieces of self-description; 'doctor' is the container, not the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimmer is a light control that varies brightness, a kind of switch.

clue.text: The two arcades have swapped entrances for stores?

indicators.note: swapped entrances means the opening letters of the two words change places

parts.note: the two is both
shopping arcades are malls

explanation.surface: Two shopping arcades exchange their doorways.
explanation.definitionFit: To mothball something is to store it away unused for a long time.

clue.text: 15's mum, also 22 24

parts.note: mum means keep quiet, which is sh
22 and 24 down are GOBLIN and TROLL; elves are also such creatures

explanation.surface: A cryptic chain of cross-references links a mother with mythical beings.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 down is MOTHBALLS, read as a verb: to put aside or postpone.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something aside indefinitely is to shelve it, a synonym of mothball.

clue.text: Witchcraft's very old circle is sealed by fate

parts.note: a circle is the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: sealed by means is sits inside the word for fate

parts.note: doom is fate

explanation.surface: Ancient magic has a circle whose fate is sealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Voodooism is the practice of voodoo, a form of sorcery.

clue.text: Catch a chill, say, where winters are very harsh

parts.note: to catch a prize is to win it
a nip is a sharp chill in the air
eg means for example, i.e. say

explanation.surface: In the bitter cold you might catch a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: This Canadian prairie city is famous for its bitterly cold winters.

clue.text: Sloth could be one with damaged retina

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: damaged shows the letters of retina are broken into a new order

explanation.surface: A slow-moving animal might be one with a damaged eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sloth' looks like the animal, but it is the sin of idleness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth means laziness, and inertia is a lack of will to act.

clue.text: Rotating rod with a bigger than usual point

parts.note: XL is the clothing size extra large
E is a compass point

explanation.surface: A rod turns about an oversized point.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is a central shaft that turns wheels.

clue.text: Kea's rotation not quite blessing in disguise

indicators.note: in disguise shows the letters are rearranged to hide their source
not quite drops the last letter of blessing

explanation.surface: A New Zealand parrot's spinning turns out to be a blessing in disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: BLESSIN (blessing less its G) joins ROTATION in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The kea is a mountain parrot whose scientific species name is this binomial.

clue.text: Young woman finally gets a bouquet

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of woman

parts.note: a bouquet is a scent, as of wine

explanation.surface: A young woman finally receives a bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouquet' looks like flowers but is the smell of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into existence, i.e. new and young.

clue.text: Spirit makes you get very drunk, mostly

parts.note: get means go, as in become

indicators.note: mostly removes the last letter

parts.note: blind drunk is very drunk

explanation.surface: Spirits will get you very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblin is a mischievous sprite, a kind of malevolent spirit.

clue.text: See 21
Fee for catching river fish

indicators.note: catching means the fee word holds the river abbreviation

parts.note: a toll is a fee

explanation.surface: Anglers pay a fee for catching fish in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To troll is to fish by trailing a baited line behind a boat.

clue.text: P&O ferries popular still?

indicators.note: ferries means carries, so the shipping firm holds the word for popular

parts.note: P&O is a ferry company; its initials give the letters
popular is hot, in demand

explanation.surface: Asks whether P&O ferries are still in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: P&O is a British ferry and cruise operator.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is a single frozen image, especially one taken from a film, i.e. a picture.

clue.text: Fence that soldiers break set down straight?

indicators.note: break means the soldiers split the enclosure

parts.note: a pen is a fenced enclosure
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Soldiers break a fence and set it upright again.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a bird smoothing its feathers flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds preen by grooming their feathers flat and neat.

clue.text: Unhealthy men in college

indicators.note: in places the soldiers inside the college word

parts.note: poly is short for polytechnic, a British college
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Students at a college have fallen ill.
explanation.walkthrough: A polytechnic was a type of British higher-education college.
explanation.definitionFit: Poorly is British informal for ill, a synonym of unhealthy.

clue.text: Some practical aid, emergency back healing

indicators.note: back tells you to read the run of letters from end to start
some means only part of the words is taken

explanation.surface: Practical help is needed in an emergency to get a back healed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a body part but is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedial treatment is intended to cure, so it is a healing kind.

clue.text: Overshoe's split — look into it

indicators.note: into puts the old word for look inside the split

parts.note: a split is a gash
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Someone's protective footwear has torn and they are told to investigate.
explanation.definitionFit: A galosh is a waterproof rubber shoe worn over another, an overshoe.

clue.text: Double hit for six, wallop crossing motorway

parts.note: to hit for six is to shock or stun, from cricket

indicators.note: crossing means the beating word straddles the road abbreviation

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to wallop them

explanation.surface: A double blow knocks someone senseless as they cross a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double' is the film stand-in, not twice. In cricket a six is the maximum single hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A stunt double replaces an actor in dangerous scenes, so a body double.
